items.text: Endurance
The night shift has ended, and a wooden plank on the cart has just cracked.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... A new plank must be located.
Remembering Partita is resting in a nearby tent, he slows his steps as he quietly searches for wood in the dark.
This isn't a trench locked in brutal conflict with the enemy.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Soldiers are unlikely to wander here. This silence is just that—silence.
A faint sob gently echoes over.
Then another, and another, the sounds stringing together into a long, fragile cord.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Partita.
He stands for a long time in the damp twilight.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: "She only cries when no one can hear."
He sets the plank down, and, with the lantern in his hand, takes a seat in front of the tent.
Her sobs grow uncontrollable, like a wounded animal.
Words from the notebook return to him. Charon carefully opens its pages.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Fabien ... he looked after all of us back then.
Charon turns the page—to the photo he tucked in there.
Amidst Partita's echoing grief, the woman in the photo smiles on.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: To whose world does this photo belong?
Trenches

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: It's been a while, Paul.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It's been only four days ... but for a major, four days is not a short time.
Eberhard smiles.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Yet it took less than that for you to get all tangled up in this Partita drama. Franz told me everything.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It is a problem indeed, but not quite so simple.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: She joined to find the truth about Walter's death, and somehow chance brought her to the right place.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: You don't think she's a witch, do you?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Likely not. A coincidence, nothing more.
His joke meets a painfully literal answer.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: If the soldiers knew the truth, they would likely start a ruckus and end up with disciplinary charges for it.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Worst case, they'd launch an ambush and maybe even end up with blood on their hands.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: But Partita isn't a soldier. She hasn't seen the true depth of human brutality.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yet she endures all that comes with war.
Eberhard stays silent, waiting for Charon to speak again.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Soldiers endure it too. Brutality is a means of survival ... and of release.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: She moves among the dead and dying, saving those who suffer.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: She even sleeps in the woods near the front, though sleep never truly comes.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: She endures fear. Endures pain. Endures rage, war ... and death.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: She's no different than a soldier.
Eberhard's face tightens. He looks away.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Is it ... bad? Partita's situation?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: "Bad" may not be the word ... "unhealthy," perhaps.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Then I'm afraid I have worse news.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: She applied for a pistol.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Did you approve it?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: It wasn't mine to approve. Lieutenant Colonel Wolker did it.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: A field nurse who buries soldiers alongside Charon requests a pistol for protection. Who would say no to that?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Even without approval, it's not hard to find a weapon at the front.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Imagine if she were forced to scavenge one and ended up with a misfiring gun ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Then it is best to give her one.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I think so.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But even a pistol requires training.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: And even with a weapon in hand, not everyone has the conviction to pull the trigger.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That's the other piece of bad news.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: She completed recruit training before she arrived. Word is, she's a natural shot.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That's why her request was approved so quickly.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... She came prepared.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: That she did.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: You still have two days until the field hospital moves out. Time enough to persuade her before the nurses rotate.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: All that might have changed her mind are dead.
The hems of their coats rise and fall with the wind, as if heaving slow, heavy breaths.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I know.
They died in war. Died in memory.
Died in the fading of every spark. Died in every stirring of dust.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: You three were like peas in a pod back then. Though, you weren't quite so affable as you are now, and Partita had an impatient streak, that's for sure.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Walter was the glue that held you together, really. He got along well with the both of you.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Whatever the case, you're the only one she might still listen to.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Because you're Paul.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It will not be easy.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Well, you can't expect me to do it. I already got one beating from Partita back in school; I'm not looking to get another.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Oh, about that photo, the one with the woman holding cornflowers—Franz has been asking around about it.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes. I ... have been trying to identify her.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Well, I think I might have a better shot at finding out than you.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Alright. Thank you.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Anything else I can help with?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is nothing. I saw Fabien at the field hospital. He is clinging to life.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: I don't think I know him ... An old friend?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Eberhard
items.text: Stay with him while you can.
Eberhard catches a faint shift in Charon's cloak. It seems as though he is nodding.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It will be done.
